$comment:
urlencoded body escaper case table, shared byte-for-byte by the three engines that build an
application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body: openbindings-go/formats/openapi,
openapi-client/go, and openapi-client/typescript/src (which openbindings-ts/packages/openapi
re-exports). Every expectation is derived from upstream authority text, never from an engine.
Each case is loaded as a WHOLE OpenAPI document through the engine's own loader, so the table
exercises the shipped path rather than a hand-built typed model.

The OAS assigns a DIFFERENT percent-encoding specification to each of the two lanes, and the
two lanes are therefore SUPPOSED to disagree about the space character. From the normatively-
cited-standards table in OAS 3.0.4 / 3.1.1 Appendix E.3 (E.4 in 3.1.2):
  [RFC6570]              style-based serialization   percent-encoding [RFC3986]
                         notes: 'does not use + for form-urlencoded'
  [RFC1866] Section 8.2.1 content-based serialization percent-encoding [RFC1738]

STYLE lane  = RFC 6570 form expansion, allowReserved not in effect: literals are RFC 3986's
              unreserved set (ALPHA / DIGIT / '-' / '.' / '_' / '~'); every other byte is
              uppercase %HH; a space is %20.
CONTENT lane = RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1 ('space characters are replaced by `+'), whose operative
              clause escapes the rest 'as per [URL]' = RFC 1738. RFC 1738 Section 2.2 permits
              'only alphanumerics, the special characters "$-_.+!*'(),", and reserved characters
              used for their reserved purposes' unencoded, names '~' among the UNSAFE characters
              that 'must always be encoded', and adds that 'characters that are not required to
              be encoded (including alphanumerics) MAY be encoded'. The engines emit the WHATWG
              form-urlencoded serializer set (ALPHA / DIGIT / '*' / '-' / '.' / '_'), which lies
              inside that permission and which OAS 3.0.4 / 3.1.1 Appendix E.3.2 (E.4.2 in 3.1.2)
              gives a SHOULD for. Which member of the permitted set the engines pick is the
              IMPLEMENTATIONS' convention, not the binding specification's.

LANE SELECTION is the OAS's own predicate, and it is PRESENCE, not truthiness. OAS 3.0.4 /
3.1.1 / 3.1.2 state it twice: the Encoding Object's closing note ('the presence of at least one
of style, explode, or allowReserved WITH AN EXPLICIT VALUE is equivalent to using schema with
in: "query" Parameter Objects. The absence of all three of those fields is the equivalent of
using content'), and Appendix E ('in the Encoding Object when at least one of style, explode,
or allowReserved is present'). OAS 3.1.0 reaches the same result through a different sentence,
carried on each of the three fields: 'If a value is explicitly defined, then the value of
contentType (implicit or explicit) SHALL be ignored.' OAS 3.0.0-3.0.3 state NEITHER sentence,
and reach the same predicate through their OWN section 4.1: 'Tooling which supports OAS 3.0
SHOULD be compatible with all OAS 3.0.* versions. The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by
tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example.' 3.0.4 is a 3.0.* version
and says outright that with all three fields absent 'Encoding is to be based on contentType
alone', so the whole 3.0 line takes the content lane for a control-free property. Until
2026-08-17 the engines instead carried a legacyOpenAPIFormEncoding predicate that put 3.0.0-
3.0.3 on the style lane, and this table's twenty 3.0.3|content cells recorded that; six of them
moved when the ruling in design/openapi-30-urlencoded-default-lane-ruling.md removed it, and
the 3.0.3|content cells are now identical to the 3.0.4|content cells by construction. That
identity is the point: the %20-versus-+ boundary is drawn between the two LANES, never between
two patch versions of one line.

EDITION DIMENSION covers each branch the engines distinguish: 3.0.3 (3.0 dialect, and the
edition whose own text states the content interpretation NOWHERE, so its rows are the ones the
patch-uniformity reading carries), 3.0.4 (3.0 dialect, the edition where the 3.0 line states
that interpretation outright and where Appendix E first appears), and 3.1.1 (3.1 dialect). The
3.0.3 and 3.0.4 rows are byte-identical after the 2026-08-17 ruling, and a diff between them is
what a reintroduced patch-version switch would produce.

The 'allow-reserved-false' declaration is the presence class: 'allowReserved: false' writes a
value that equals the field's default, so a typed model that stores it as a plain boolean cannot
tell it from an absent field. It selects the STYLE lane on every edition that states the
predicate, and its cells are red against any engine that reads truthiness instead of presence.

Each case declares one urlencoded request body with exactly one property; `expect` is the whole
emitted body, which all three engines must produce byte for byte.
